summary: Ustaz Azlan tells the story of Surah An-Najm: in Ramadan the Prophet SAW suddenly recited it at the Sacred Mosque and everyone present, Quraysh included, prostrated except Umayyah ibn Khalaf. Quraysh then invented the 'gharaniq verses' story to save face, and a false report that Quraysh had become Muslim reached the emigrants in Abyssinia. Some returned; Uthman ibn Maz'un took Al-Walid's protection but gave it back and had his eye bruised. The second migration followed, with 83 men and 28 women led by Ja'far. The ustaz walks through the Quraysh envoys (Amr ibn Al-As and Abdullah ibn Abi Rabi'ah) to the Najashi, Ja'far's speech, the recitation of Surah Maryam, the Najashi's ruling, how he became king, the Prophet's letter, and the Prophet's absentee funeral prayer for him.
keyPoints: The Prophet SAW recited Surah An-Najm suddenly and all present prostrated except Umayyah ibn Khalaf, who only took soil to his forehead.
Quraysh saved face with the gharaniq story; the false news that Quraysh were Muslim reached Abyssinia and some emigrants returned.
Uthman ibn Maz'un gave up Al-Walid's protection because he would not live in peace while his companions were tortured.
The second migration was 83 men and 28 women under Ja'far ibn Abi Talib.
The Quraysh envoys won over the Najashi's ministers with gifts, but the Najashi refused to rule before hearing Ja'far.
Ja'far gave a crafted speech summing up Islam and recited Surah Maryam, stating that Isa is a servant of Allah and His word; the Najashi drew a line on a stick and guaranteed their safety.
The Najashi accepted Islam in secret, and the Prophet SAW prayed over him in absentia when he died.

lessons.title: Allah preserves the Quran's miracle
lessons.body: The Quran's miracle lasts until the Last Day, unlike miracles only witnessed at the time.

lessons.title: Read to understand
lessons.body: Learn the meaning of what is recited in prayer so the miracle is felt.

lessons.title: Longing for the Prophet SAW above homeland
lessons.body: The emigrants returned out of longing for the Prophet SAW, above longing for family.

lessons.title: Solidarity over comfort
lessons.body: Uthman gave up protection because it was unfair for him to be safe while companions were tortured.

lessons.title: Islamic brotherhood over tribal ties
lessons.body: The bond of Islam is higher than the bond of family.

lessons.title: Social capital and exposure
lessons.body: Company and exposure build leadership, like Amr and the Prophet with Abdul Muttalib.

lessons.title: Understand lobbying
lessons.body: Lobbying behind power shapes policy; Amr won the ministers before meeting the king.

lessons.title: A well-crafted speech
lessons.body: Ja'far began with before-and-after, avoided sensitive issues and stated what Islam is.

lessons.title: Say what Islam is, not only what it is not
lessons.body: Ja'far only said Isa is a servant and word of Allah without attacking.

lessons.title: A just leader refuses bribes
lessons.body: The Najashi returned the gifts because Allah took no bribe from him.

lessons.title: Every small good is multiplied
lessons.body: The Najashi's kindness flows to African Muslims and Egyptian scholars today.

Relationships and exposure that open opportunities.

dalil.context: Surah An-Najm, recited suddenly by the Prophet SAW at the Sacred Mosque.
dalil.translation: By the star when it sets!

dalil.context: Which of your Lord's blessings do you doubt?
dalil.translation: Which then of your Lord’s blessings do you deny?

dalil.context: The near Hour has drawn close.
A rebuke to those who are amazed at the Quran while laughing at it.
Prostrate to Allah and worship Him; the prostration of recitation.
dalil.translation: Bow down before God and worship.

dalil.context: Allah made the Quran easy for remembrance.
dalil.translation: We have made it easy to learn lessons from the Quran: will anyone take heed?

dalil.context: Sahih Bukhari via Ibn Abbas; Uthman was struck until his eye was bruised.
dalil.translation: Labid said 'everything besides Allah is false'; Uthman agreed, but objected to 'every blessing will vanish', since the blessings of paradise will not vanish.

dalil.context: Answer to Umar, who teased Asma' that they were closer to the Prophet SAW.
dalil.translation: The Prophet SAW told Asma' bint Umays that they had migrated twice.

dalil.context: A weak report cited in the sirah books.
dalil.translation: Uthman was the first to migrate with his family since Lut AS.

dalil.context: The verse said to refer to the Najashi: eyes overflowing with tears at the truth.
dalil.translation: and when they listen to what has been sent down to the Messenger, you will see their eyes overflowing with tears because they recognize the Truth [in it]. They say, ‘Our Lord, we believe, so count us amongst the witnesses.

dalil.context: The call to a common word in the Prophet's letter to the Najashi.
dalil.translation: Say, ‘People of the Book, let us arrive at a statement that is common to us all: we worship God alone, we ascribe no partner to Him, and none of us takes others beside God as lords.’ If they turn away, say, ‘Witness our devotion to Him.’
